pages.x: Saint-Domingue, the French half of Hispaniola, grew more sugar and coffee than any other colony on Earth. About 500,000 enslaved Africans worked its plantations under some 40,000 whites, and so many died that ships brought tens of thousands more every year.

In August 1791 enslaved leaders met at a night ceremony in the forest of Bois Caiman, led, tradition says, by a Vodou priest, Dutty Boukman. Days later the plantations of the northern plain went up in flames, in the largest slave revolt in history.

A formerly enslaved coachman, Toussaint Louverture, became the greatest general of the revolt. When France abolished slavery in 1794 he joined the French and drove out the Spanish and British invaders. By 1801 he governed the whole island.

Napoleon wanted the colony, and slavery, back. In 1802 he sent General Leclerc with a great army, and yellow fever killed most of it, Leclerc too. Toussaint was lured into talks, arrested, and died in a cold French prison in 1803.
pages.of: French soldiers dead, most of fever

pages.x: When it was clear that France meant to bring back slavery, Toussaint's general Jean-Jacques Dessalines led the war to the end. On 18 November 1803 his army beat the French at Vertières, and they left the island.

On 1 January 1804 Dessalines declared independence and gave the country its old Taíno name, Haiti. It was the first nation founded by people who had freed themselves from slavery, and the second free country in the Americas.
Under slavery, pumpkin soup was a dish for the masters. Every 1 January, Haitians eat soup joumou, pumpkin soup, to celebrate their freedom.

The great powers shunned the new black republic. In 1825 France, with warships off the coast, made Haiti pay 150 million francs to former slave owners in return for recognition. Haiti was still paying off the loans in the 1940s.

The Haitian Revolution was the only slave revolt in history that founded a nation. It frightened slave owners across the Americas and inspired enslaved people and abolitionists everywhere, and it helped persuade Napoleon to sell Louisiana to the United States.
pts: The largest slave revolt in history, 1791
